channel.title: Arc Poetry Magazine - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Arc Poetry Magazine (arcpoetry.ca)

item.title: Fear is a city in every woman: Yvonne Blomer’s Death of Persephone
item.description: Yvonne Blomer’s Death of Persephone is a murder mystery in verse set in the present day with main characters demonstrating ancient Greek literary devices.

item.title: Language as Music: Joseph Maviglia’s In a Cage of Sunlight
item.description: Joseph Maviglia’s poetry is about ordinary life, people, working-class society, social justice, and being an immigrant in Canada’s effervescent cultural mosaic.

item.title: Changing with the tide: Melanie Marttila’s The Art of Floating
item.description: Nature is intertwined with family lore and love in Melanie Marttila's debut poetry book, and with myth, ancient magic and feminism to summon mystery.

item.title: Growing Through Grief: Jessica Bebenek’s No One Knows Us There
item.description: Split in two parts, Jessica Bebenek’s debut poetry collection, No One Knows Us There, reflects on the grief of end-of-life care over the course of a decade.

item.title: The Imaginative Superpower: Carol Krause’s A Bouquet of Glass
item.description: The author’s obsession with an ordinary world originates out of her inability to abide and live inside its confines. This book accepts that fact, looking for what’s on the other side.

item.title: Loss and Discovery of Self Through Language
item.description: In Kyo Lee's debut collection, language is inadequate while navigating queerness at the intersection of Korean heritage, familial expectation, and coming of age.

item.title: Constructing the Body in Verse
item.description: In jaye simpson's a body more tolerable, the poet chews over existence in a body that must be perceived, a body that refuses being ignored or rewritten.

item.title: Who’s Afraid of Orpheus and Eurydice? Part 2
item.description: The Xenotext: Book 2 is the culmination of Christian Bök’s 25-year project. I can assure those who enjoyed the first volume they will not be disappointed.

item.title: Midway This Life: Kayla Czaga’s Midway
item.description: To call Midway an elegiac work is both understatement and truism. Kayla Czaga’s literary examination of paternal loss merits all the breadth she grants it.

item.title: Mingled Beyond Parting in Tamil Terrains
item.description: Tamil Terrains, edited by Nedra Rodrigo and Geetha Sukumaran, is a tender and evocative collection of Tamil poetry and translations.
